about: Every codec name CPython 3.14.5 knows (encodings.aliases keys and values and every encodings module): what CPython does with `# coding: <name>` followed by `x = 1`, the codec it resolves to, whether another module can take the name over at run time, and the outcome each reader must report. Generated by gen_pep263_vectors.py; never edited by hand.
policy: Owner decision D2 (default 'expect'): plain/transparent -> every reader evaluates; foreign -> the Python engine decodes, Semgrep and secrets record lost evaluation; unknown -> lost everywhere; refused -> any outcome. 'expect_under_d2a' is the corrected D2-A (OWNER-DECISIONS §0.8): only takeover-immune spellings stay UTF-8-equivalent. A taken-over, non-immune name (takeover-* vectors) is D2's documented false clean ('d2_documented_false_clean'), asserted lost only under D2-A (OR-59). No outcome may crash the Python engine (OR-53). Paths measured: import (compile(bytes)+exec), script, and python -x (OR-49).
normalisation: A cookie name reaches a codec the way CPython 3.14.5 sends it: the tokenizer's get_normal_name looks at the first 12 characters with '_' read as '-' and letters lower-cased; 'utf-8' and 'utf-8-*' become utf-8, 'latin-1', 'iso-8859-1', 'iso-latin-1' and their '-*' forms become iso-8859-1, and those names are decoded on a C fast path that no run-time registration reaches. Every other name, unchanged, goes to codecs.lookup, which lower-cases it and lets encodings.search_function collapse each run of characters other than letters, digits and '.' into '_' before reading encodings.aliases. Rows with 'variant_of' are case and separator variants of a base name; every verdict and takeover_immune value here is measured, not derived from this description.

control.rule: every tree a name is tested in also holds this plain file, and its finding must be reported (OR-53)
